entity.summary: Seychelles-registered centralized cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2018 and continuing globally. Bitget announced a phased exit from Japan in August 2026; after a September 24 security incident temporarily disrupted withdrawals, the phased restoration of crypto withdrawals, fiat, and P2P/C2C services was completed on October 2.
entity.notes: On 2026-09-24 at 18:31 UTC, Bitget detected unauthorized transfers affecting a limited portion of its hot and warm wallet layers. The estimated impacted amount was revised to approximately USD 387.5 million. Bitget's investigation states that attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to obtain intranet access credentials and forge withdrawal commands; private keys were not compromised and cold wallets were not affected. Independent XRPL analysis reports 102,976,680 XRP transferred from Bitget-labeled wallets during the incident. Bitget says the vulnerability was remediated and the incident contained. BTC withdrawals resumed on 2026-09-28, ETH on 2026-09-29, USDT on 2026-09-30, and on 2026-10-02 Bitget confirmed that withdrawals for other supported tokens together with fiat and P2P/C2C services had resumed, completing the phased restoration plan. HEI therefore returns the global exchange status to active. Asset tracing, recovery, and post-incident security work may continue without implying an operational limitation. Operational restoration was rechecked against Bitget's October 2 completion notice on 2026-10-08.

events.title: Bitget began operating
events.description: Bitget began operating as a centralized cryptocurrency exchange in 2018.
events.notes: Year-level launch marker based on official company history.

events.title: BitKeep joined the Bitget ecosystem
events.description: Bitget announced a strategic transaction that brought BitKeep into the wider Bitget ecosystem.
events.notes: BitKeep later rebranded as Bitget Wallet. The event did not change the active status of the Bitget exchange.

events.title: Bitget announced the end of services for residents of Japan
events.description: Bitget announced that it would cease serving residents of Japan, stop new registrations after 2026-08-03, place affected accounts in close-only mode from 2026-11-01, and forcibly close remaining positions from 2026-12-31 while keeping withdrawals available.
events.notes: This is a regional service withdrawal for residents of Japan. It does not establish a global shutdown or change Bitget's entity status from active.

events.title: Bitget confirmed unauthorized transfers from hot and warm wallet layers
events.description: Bitget said its security systems detected unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC affecting a limited portion of its hot and warm wallet infrastructure. The exchange later revised the affected amount from approximately USD 351.6 million to approximately USD 387.5 million after classifying additional affected assets on Zcash and TRON. Bitget later said attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to steal intranet access credentials and forge withdrawal commands that bypassed risk verification; private keys were not compromised.
events.notes: Bitget said the incident was contained, the underlying vulnerability was remediated, and no further unauthorized transfers were possible. Cold wallets were not affected. Confirmed affected networks/assets include Ethereum and multiple EVM networks, XRP Ledger, Zcash, and TRON. Independent XRPL analysis reports 102,976,680 XRP transferred from Bitget-labeled wallets during the incident. Investigation, tracing and recovery work with Mandiant and SlowMist remain ongoing.

events.title: Bitget temporarily suspended withdrawals pending security review
events.description: Bitget temporarily paused withdrawals as a precaution while reviewing the September 24 wallet security incident. A phased restoration plan was then announced, with BTC withdrawals confirmed open again on September 28 and broader restoration scheduled through October 2.
events.notes: This was a platform-wide temporary withdrawal suspension tied to the September 24 incident. Partial restoration began on September 28. HEI keeps the entity limited until broad withdrawal restoration is confirmed.

events.title: Bitget began phased withdrawal restoration
events.description: Bitget confirmed that BTC withdrawals on the Bitcoin and BSC networks reopened at 08:00 UTC on September 28 after additional security validation. ETH, USDT, other supported tokens, fiat and P2P services were scheduled to resume progressively through October 2.
events.notes: This is partial restoration rather than full platform normalization. The entity remains limited pending confirmation that withdrawal service has broadly returned.

events.title: Bitget completed phased withdrawal and related-service restoration
events.description: Bitget announced that withdrawals for supported tokens other than BTC, ETH, and USDT had resumed together with fiat and P2P/C2C services, completing the phased restoration plan that followed the September 24 security incident.
events.notes: BTC, ETH, and USDT withdrawals had already resumed on September 28, September 29, and September 30 respectively. The October 2 update closes the operational withdrawal-restoration sequence. Ongoing asset tracing or post-incident security work does not by itself keep the exchange in limited status.

evidence.notes: Official announcement records the Bitget and BitKeep transaction.

evidence.notes: Official follow-up records the BitKeep rebrand as Bitget Wallet.

evidence.title: Announcement: Important Notice for Japanese Residents
evidence.notes: First-party announcement confirms the phased end of services for residents of Japan, registration cutoff, account-restriction schedule, and forced position closure schedule.

evidence.title: FAQ - Important notice for Japanese Residents
evidence.notes: First-party FAQ specifies close-only restrictions from 2026-11-01, forced liquidation from 2026-12-31, and continuing withdrawal availability.

evidence.title: Bitget Hot Wallet Incident — September 24, 2026
evidence.notes: First-party security notice states that unauthorized transfers were detected at 18:31 UTC, estimates approximately USD 351.6 million affected, says the breach was limited to portions of hot and warm wallet layers, says cold wallets remained secure, states the User Protection Fund held more than USD 464 million and covered the loss, confirms a temporary withdrawal suspension while deposits/trading stayed operational, and promises a full incident report with root-cause analysis and corrective actions within 24 hours.

evidence.title: Bitget confirms $351M security breach, suspends withdrawals
evidence.notes: Independent report reflecting Bitget's later confirmation of approximately USD 351.6 million affected and the hot/warm-wallet scope.

evidence.title: Nearly $352M Moved From Crypto Exchange Bitget Wallets in Suspected Hack
evidence.notes: Independent coverage quoting Bitget's CEO and reporting that withdrawals were temporarily paused while deposits and trading remained operational.

evidence.title: Bitget acknowledges $351.6M outflow incident and temporarily suspends withdrawals
evidence.notes: Independent report summarizing Bitget's first-party notice, including the temporary withdrawal suspension and continued deposit/trading availability.

evidence.title: Important updates on the September 24 Bitget security incident
evidence.notes: First-party update revises the affected amount to approximately USD 387.5 million after adding affected Zcash and TRON assets, says the revision does not represent additional unauthorized transfers, states that the incident is contained with no further unauthorized transfers possible, identifies affected networks/assets, names Mandiant and SlowMist as investigation partners, confirms withdrawals remain suspended, and says a withdrawal plan will be announced by 2026-09-26 04:00 UTC.

evidence.title: Bitget Security Incident — Official Progress Update
evidence.notes: First-party incident hub states that a third-party security-product vulnerability exposed intranet credentials used to forge withdrawal commands, that private keys were not compromised, and that the vulnerability was remediated.

evidence.title: Bitget Hack Leaves $157 Million in XRP Beyond Freeze Controls
evidence.notes: Independent report based on XRPL transaction history states that 102,976,680 XRP moved from Bitget-labeled wallets in three successful transfers.

evidence.title: Bitget Security Incident: Timeline, Impact and Response (Updated)
evidence.notes: First-party update confirms BTC withdrawals on Bitcoin and BSC reopened at 08:00 UTC on September 28 and describes the remaining phased restoration schedule.

evidence.title: Bitget announcement on completing the phased resumption of token withdrawals, fiat, and C2C services
evidence.notes: First-party support notice states that withdrawals for other tokens, fiat, and C2C services resumed and that the previously announced phased resumption plan was fully completed.

evidence.title: Bitget Security Incident: Timeline, Impact and Response
evidence.notes: First-party incident follow-up states that Bitget completed its phased withdrawal-resumption plan on October 2, following BTC, ETH, and USDT restoration on the preceding dates.
